provenance.note: Split-vintage regional series: Greater Mumbai's Mithi carries real 2018-2023 WQ (CPCB NWMP station series via Praja 2024 + the MPCB Mithi Action Plan); the eastern Ulhas corridor carries the 2004-05 MPCB Kalyan-Region ESR baseline and remains a CPCB priority/polluted stretch; the source rivers are context-only. _readings_status and _wqr_source carry the per-river population state; FC units are inconsistent across MPCB editions - directional only (registry note).

source: Regional MMR rivers. Greater Mumbai's Mithi carries real 2018-2023 WQ (CPCB NWMP via Praja 2024 + MPCB 2019 Mithi Action Plan). The eastern Ulhas corridor carries a 2004-05 MPCB Kalyan-Region ESR baseline (BOD 3-8, DO 5.7-7.9 at Badlapur) and remains a CPCB priority/polluted stretch with the Waldhuni tributary adding Ulhasnagar industrial effluent. The source rivers (Vaitarna/Bhatsa/Tansa/Surya/Kalu) are upstream of the supply reservoirs and shown for context, not WQ. Dahisar/Poisar/Oshiwara are unmonitored. mpcb.gov.in / cpcb.gov.in/nwmp-data.

rivers.name: Mithi River
rivers.description: Mumbai's principal river. It rises from the Vihar and Powai lake overflows in the Sanjay Gandhi National Park and runs about 18 km south-west through Saki Naka, Kurla, Dharavi and Mahim before emptying into the Arabian Sea at Mahim Creek. Walled and channelised along most of its length, it carries largely untreated sewage and industrial effluent, and it was the river that overflowed in the 26 July 2005 deluge. CPCB lists the Mithi among India's most polluted (Priority I) river stretches.
rivers.notes: Governed by the Mithi River Development and Protection Authority (MRDPA, constituted 2005) and the subject of a 2025 Enforcement Directorate money-laundering probe into desilting contracts. Water-quality readings pending (see source). MPCB's own annual averages confirm the worsening: station 2168's average BOD ran 45 mg/l in 2018-19 and 53 in 2023-24 - the worst year in the series - with dissolved oxygen at 2-4 mg/l and a Water Quality Index of 32. readings.fecal_coliform_note: CPCB's official figure, shown as published. Praja Foundation, transcribing the same CPCB series, flags the 100x jump from 5,400 (2022) as a likely recording error ('seems like an error'). Treat the magnitude as directional; either way the Mithi is far beyond the bathing standard.

mpcb_wqr_series._note: Annual AVERAGES for station 2168 (Mithi at Mahim bridge) from MPCB's annual 'Water Quality Status of Maharashtra' reports - a different statistic from the stations' annual-maxima readings. The 2019-20 report was never published (gap year). Faecal-coliform excluded (units print inconsistently across editions). WQI 2023-24 = 32 (Mumbai RO Table 37).
mpcb_wqr_series.source: MPCB Water Quality Status of Maharashtra, annual reports 2018-19 to 2023-24

rivers.name: Dahisar River
rivers.description: Rises from Tulsi Lake in the Sanjay Gandhi National Park and flows about 12 km west through Dahisar to the Gorai/Manori Creek and the Arabian Sea. Through built-up Dahisar it runs as a sewage-fed channel. CPCB lists it among the polluted river stretches; the BMC has floated rejuvenation tenders since 2022, with two sewage-treatment plants under trial in 2025.
rivers.notes: A focus of the citizen 'River March' campaign for clean Mumbai rivers.

rivers.name: Poisar River
rivers.description: Originates in the Sanjay Gandhi National Park and runs about 7 km through Kandivali to the Marve Creek and the Arabian Sea. Through built-up Kandivali it has been reduced largely to a storm-water and sewage channel. CPCB lists it among the polluted river stretches.
rivers.notes: Part of the BMC's four-river rejuvenation programme.

rivers.name: Oshiwara River
rivers.description: Rises near the Aarey Milk Colony and the Sanjay Gandhi National Park and flows about 7 km through Goregaon and Jogeshwari to the Malad Creek and the Arabian Sea. Heavily encroached and sewage-fed through its urban course. CPCB lists it among the polluted river stretches.
rivers.notes: Part of the BMC's four-river rejuvenation programme.

rivers.name: Ulhas River
rivers.description: The eastern MMR's lifeline and its wound: the river that (via MIDC/STEM lifts) supplies Thane, Kalyan-Dombivli, Ulhasnagar and Bhiwandi also receives their largely-untreated sewage. It rises near Lonavla and flows past Karjat, Badlapur, Ambernath and Ulhasnagar to Vasai Creek. MPCB classifies it in stretches (A-I origin to Badlapur, A-II to the NRC bund at Shahad, SW-II to the sea).
rivers.notes: Among India's polluted river stretches; the Waldhuni tributary adds Ulhasnagar's industrial effluent. The reading below is a 2004-05 baseline (MPCB Kalyan Region ESR); current routine monitoring is sparse. MPCB's annual averages 2018-19 to 2023-24 show the Ulhas mainstem consistently within norms (BOD around 3 mg/l, DO around 7) at Badlapur, Mohane and Jambhul - the crisis sits in the unmonitored Waldhuni tributary and in the creeks (Thane Creek at Kalwa averaged BOD ~14 in the last two report years). rivers.name: Waldhuni River
rivers.description: A short, heavily polluted tributary nalla through Ulhasnagar and Ambernath that collects industrial effluent (dyeing and chemical units) and untreated sewage before joining the Ulhas - one of the MMR's most chemically degraded stretches.
rivers.notes: Recurrent froth and fish-kill events; an NGT-monitored stretch. Quantitative readings pending.

rivers.name: Kalu River
rivers.cpcb_class: Water-supply source river (upstream; not a CPCB polluted stretch)
rivers.description: An Ulhas tributary in the eastern Ghats. The planned 1,140 MLD Kalu dam (KIDC, MMRDA-funded) would impound it to augment the eastern corridor's bulk supply.
rivers.notes: Upstream source; the dam is contested on forest-submergence grounds.

rivers.name: Vaitarna River
rivers.cpcb_class: Water-supply source river (upstream; not a CPCB polluted stretch)
rivers.description: The principal source river for Greater Mumbai, impounded by the Upper Vaitarna, Middle Vaitarna and Modak Sagar dams in the Western Ghats before piped supply to BMC.

rivers.name: Bhatsa River
rivers.cpcb_class: Water-supply source river (upstream; not a CPCB polluted stretch)
rivers.description: Impounded by Bhatsa dam in Shahapur, Thane - BMC's single largest source (~48% of Greater Mumbai's water).

rivers.name: Surya River
rivers.cpcb_class: Water-supply source river (upstream; not a CPCB polluted stretch)
rivers.description: The Palghar source for the western corridor, impounded by Surya (Dhamni) dam - the raw source for MMRDA's 403 MLD Surya scheme serving Vasai-Virar and Mira-Bhayandar.

rivers.name: Tansa River
rivers.cpcb_class: Water-supply source river (upstream; not a CPCB polluted stretch)
rivers.description: Impounded by Tansa dam in Shahapur, one of BMC's older Western-Ghats sources.
